blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: As AI generated images are getting popular these days, discussions on such generations are widely existed in current public forums, software repositories, and photography tutorials. Moreover, with the help of LLM-assisted code translation, malicious actors can adopt such information to evade detectors without specialized knowledge or local GPU execution of the resulting tools. To evaluate such risks, we introduce \textsc{WildFakeToolBench}, a benchmark suite of $156$ executable image-processing tools derived from $220$ public sources across $142$ domains. Each tool retains its source evidence and passes syntax, execution, and output-distortion checks without using feedback from the evaluated detectors. On $105$ generated images from five generators, we evaluate six state-of-the-art detectors with images processed by the tools in our collected bench to assess their effectiveness against such in-the-wild risks. The strongest individual tools achieve attack success rates of $25.25\%$--$100\%$ across detectors, exceeding the strongest of six selected image-processing baselines for each detector. Evaluating subsets of an eight-tool pool yields worst-case coverage above $80\%$ for every detector. Effectiveness is sparse and detector-specific: high coverage across candidates does not imply reliable one-shot evasion. These findings not only highlight the potential of such web-sourced risks, but also show the potential on establishing AI-image detector robustness evaluation framework based on those in-the-wild information.

blocks.en: Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: As AI-generated images become increasingly accessible, more users are discussing them online. However, these images can also be used for malicious purposes, such as spreading misinformation. Although several detectors have been proposed to identify statistical, frequency-domain, or visual-artifact cues, prior work has shown that their robustness against various attacks remains limited [ 5 , 11 , 25 ] . Moreover, malicious actors can draw on publicly accessible web knowledge about photographic appearance, camera artifacts, and detector evasion. With the help of current LLMs, they can translate this knowledge into image-processing operations that make generated images evade detectors. Because these operations can be applied by non-experts with image-processing knowledge using only a CPU, this risk should not be overlooked.
blocks.zh: 随着AI生成的图像越来越容易取用,更多用户在网上讨论. 然而,这些图像也可用于恶意目的,例如传播错误信息. 虽然已提出数个探测器来识别统计、频域或视觉艺术提示,但先前的研究表明,它们抵御各种攻击的力度仍然有限[5、11、25]。 此外,恶意行为者可以利用公众可获取的关于相片外观、相机文物和探测器逃逸的网络知识。 在目前LLMs的帮助下,他们可以将这种知识转化为图像处理操作,使所生成的图像逃避探测器. 由于这些操作可以被只有CPU的图像处理知识的非专家所应用,因此这种风险不应该被忽略.

blocks.en: Such knowledge is distributed across forums, software repositories, image-tool sites, and photography tutorials. Some sources explicitly discuss evasion, while others describe ordinary editing or simulated capture effects. Although these sources often provide informal descriptions rather than directly applicable code or software, attackers can use LLMs to translate them into runnable code, reducing the implementation expertise required. Most resulting transformations can also be performed with standard image-processing libraries on CPUs. The relevant question is therefore whether accessible public experience can supply effective robustness tests for current detectors, even without detector-specific attack optimization.
blocks.zh: 这种知识分布在论坛、软件库、图像工具站点和摄影教程中。 一些来源明确讨论逃逸,而另一些来源则描述普通编辑或模拟捕获效果. 虽然这些来源往往提供非正式的描述,而不是直接适用的代码或软件,但攻击者可以使用LLMS将其翻译为可运行代码,从而减少所需的执行专业知识. 大多数由此而来的变化也可以在CPU上与标准图像处理库一起进行. 因此,相关问题是,可获得的公众经验能否为目前的探测器提供有效的强性测试,即使没有针对探测器的攻击优化.

blocks.en: We introduce WildFakeToolBench , a suite of 156 156 executable tools with source provenance and a common evaluation protocol. The tools are generated by our WildFake agent framework, which performs text retrieval, method extraction, deduplication, and code generation. They span ten categories, including artifact repair, color adjustment, resampling, and simulated capture effects. To reflect attackers with limited resources, the image-processing operations in our benchmark require no local GPU. Neither tool synthesis nor image-specific parameter proposals use detector feedback. Our contribution is the resulting benchmark resource and its assessment of an accessible processing space, rather than a new detector-specific optimization algorithm.

blocks.en:
To measure the robustness of current state-of-the-art AI detectors in our settings, we evaluate six state-of-the-art AI detectors after processing our collected tools on an image set collected across five generators and seven content categories.
For each tool and image, we process the tool with five parameter candidates generated by GPT-4o-mini and retain outputs with SSIM at least 0.75 0.75 .
Based on the evaluation, we find that every evaluated detector is vulnerable to at least one tool, and the strongest individual tool exceeds the strongest of six selected baselines for each detector.
Although most tools cannot effectively affect the prediction of the state-of-the-art detectors, we still find many useful tools for current detectors. For example, the maximum single-tool attack success rate (ASR) for FakeVLM is 45.54 % 45.54\% , demonstrating substantial weaknesses for current detectors.

对于每个工具和图像,我们用GPT-4o-mini生成的5个参数候选人处理工具,并保留SSIM至少0.75 0.75的输出.
根据评价,我们发现每个被评价的探测器都至少容易受到一个工具的伤害,最强的单个工具超过每个探测器六个选定基线中最强的.
虽然大多数工具无法有效地影响对最先进的探测器的预测,但我们仍然能找到许多用于当前探测器的有用工具. 例如,FakeVLM的最大单工具攻击成功率(ASR)为45.54% 45.54\%X,表明当前探测器存在重大弱点.

blocks.en:
Besides single-tools, malicious actors may also collect several attack tools, combine them for effective attacks.
Therefore, we also evaluate the coverage obtained by trying subsets of several available tools.
It exposes broader weaknesses, but measures a worst-case candidate portfolio rather than one-shot evasion.
Since the combination of all tools are too many, we select a candidate pool from our single-tool evaluation to our coverage evaluation.
Besides the measurement on the risks, our in-the-wild analysis also traces how public sources contribute executable methods and how tool categories and source types appear among effective candidates. Our contributions are threefold: • We introduce WildFakeToolBench , a benchmark of 156 156 executable, provenance-linked image-processing tools derived from public web knowledge, with CPU-compatible implementations and shared validity checks. • We evaluate six AI-image detectors under single-tool and multiple-candidate protocols, revealing substantial but detector-specific weaknesses beyond six selected image-processing baselines. • We analyze the conversion of public knowledge into tools, the processing strategies it covers, and the sources represented among effective tools, providing a basis for reproducible robustness testing.

blocks.zh: 相关工作

blocks.en: AI Image Generators
blocks.zh: AI 图像生成器

blocks.en:
AI image generation has progressed through several modeling paradigms, making
high-quality synthesis increasingly accessible. Early generative adversarial
networks [ 9 , 15 , 30 ] often produced lower-fidelity images. Therefore, diffusion [ 12 , 28 ] and latent-diffusion models [ 24 ] subsequently became dominant,
particularly for high-fidelity text-to-image synthesis [ 22 , 1 ] , and attracted
substantial public attention.
However, diffusion models can still struggle to follow complex user prompts, limiting their utility for some practical tasks.
Newer generation systems, such as GPT-Image and Nano Banana [ 18 , 8 , 17 ] , improve prompt understanding with their internal language models [ 4 , 16 ] while producing high-quality images.
This evolution is relevant to detection because different generator families may leave different color, spectral, or processing artifacts.
We therefore include five popular generators in our evaluation.

blocks.en: AI-Generated Image Detectors

blocks.en:
AI-generated images can be used to spread rumors and misinformation online,
potentially causing substantial social harm. Researchers have therefore
developed detectors to distinguish AI-generated images from real ones [ 10 ] .
Traditional neural-classifier-based detectors are commonly trained on large
datasets of generated images [ 26 , 21 ] or on specific artifacts
associated with image generation [ 35 , 36 , 7 ] . Some methods leverage the
generator models themselves for zero-shot fake-image
classification [ 27 ] .

blocks.en: Threat Model
blocks.zh: 威胁模式

blocks.en:
As AI models are easily accessible for common people, we now consider a non-professional, in-the-wild malicious actor who seeks to make an AI-generated image evade detection by having it classified as real.
The actor can search publicly available online knowledge and use a general-purpose LLM to translate relevant advice into image-processing tools, but is not assumed to have specialized image-forensics expertise or local GPU resources.
The actor can submit images to a black-box detector and observe its binary decision (real or AI-generated).
The detector’s identity and all other information—including its architecture, parameters, training data, confidence scores, and decision threshold—are unknown to the actor. Thus, the threat model permits only label-level feedback, not white-box access or detector-specific knowledge.

由于AI模型对于普通人来说是容易获得的,我们现在考虑的是一位非专业的,一丝不苟的恶意演员,他试图通过将AI生成的图像归为真实而使图像被检测出逃避.
演员可以搜索公开的在线知识,并使用通用的LLM来将相關建議被翻译成图像处理工具,但被假定没有专门的图像法专门知识或本地GPU资源.
演员可以向黑盒探测器提交图像并观察其二进制决定(真或AI生成).
探测器的身份和所有其他信息 -- -- 包括其结构、参数、培训数据、信心分数和决定门槛 -- -- 对行为者来说是未知的。 因此,威胁模型只允许标签级反馈,而不是白箱访问或检测器特定知识.

blocks.en: Benchmark Collection Framework
blocks.zh: 基准收集框架

blocks.en:
To collect web-based tools can be utilized by malicious actors, we build a agent framework called WildFake by simulating the actors’ operation on collecting knowledge and converting them to applicable tools.
The framework contains three stages as follow, • Retrieval and Knowledge Processing: We first adopt Tavily to collect knowledge about AI-generated images from public sources. Then we adopt GPT-4o-mini to preprocess the collected texts, removing the low quality terms like short and out-of-scope texts. And we finally formulate them in a constant template for provenance. • Method Extraction and Deduplication: After collected the information, we adopt GPT-4o-mini to extract actionable methods and other information related to the method for further analysis, like quoted evidence. Then we also adopt the model to identify the repeated techniques and merge them to preserve the unique tools for our benchmark. • Tool Synthesis and Validation: After extracted the methods, we adopt GPT-4o-mini to convert the retained method into a parameterized Python image-processing tool. Since our threat models targets on the non-professional attackers, our generated image-processor are all applicable for CPU tools as such attackers usually do not have sufficient GPU resources for diffusion or other techniques. We also check the tools by evaluating their interface validity, execution, non-identity output, and distortion. Failures can be revised using software diagnostics without detector feedback.

blocks.en: The Obtained WildFakeToolBench
blocks.zh: 获取的"野生假人"Bench

blocks.en:
As shown in the right part of Figure 1 , our obtained WildFakeToolBench contains 156 156 validated tools derived from 220 220 public sources across 142 142 domains. These synthesized image-processing operations use standard libraries and require no local GPU.
The tools retain source provenance and executable implementations, and are organized into ten categories spanning operations such as color adjustment, resampling, and simulated capture effects, details are described in Appendix B .
Their goals fall into broader patterns: reducing recognizable synthetic appearance through detail repair, de-stylization, and texture changes; adjusting lighting and color; adding simulated capture cues through analog effects, lens effects, noise, and reframing; and reproducing resizing or re-encoding associated with image sharing.

blocks.en: Settings of our Benchmark Evaluation
blocks.zh: 基准评价的设置

blocks.en: We evaluate four VLM-based systems, FakeVLM [ 32 ] , SIDA-13B [ 13 ] , FakeShield [ 34 ] , and GPT-5.6-luna [ 20 ] , and two neural classifiers, CommForensics [ 21 ] and AIDE [ 35 ] . We use FakeShield ’s DTE-FDM component for classification and prompt GPT-5.6-luna directly. Additional detector descriptions and the prompt appear in Appendices C.1 and E.6 .
blocks.zh: 我们评价四个基于VLM的系统,即:假VLM [32],SIDA-13B [13],假盾 [34],和GPT-5.6-luna [20],以及两个神经分类器,Commerforensics [21]和AIDE [35]. 我们使用假盾的DTE-FDM组件进行分类, 附加的探测器描述和快取出现在附录C.1和E.6中.

blocks.en: We compare against six selected image-processing baselines: Gaussian/salt-and-pepper noise, spectral suppression, defocus blur, Poisson–Gaussian noise, simulated camera processing, and Reinhard color transfer [ 11 , 33 , 6 , 3 , 23 ] . All use the same candidate and distortion-filtering protocol. This comparison measures additional stress-testing value relative to these implementations, rather than superiority over all academic attacks. Details appear in Appendix C.2 .
blocks.zh: 我们比较了六个选定的图像处理基线:高斯/盐-和-上位噪音、光谱抑制、去焦模糊度、波森-高斯噪音、模拟相机处理和Reinhard色调[11、33、6、3、23]。 都使用相同的候选和扭曲过滤协议. 这种比较衡量了与这些执行相比的额外压力测试价值,而不是高于所有学术攻击。 详情见附录C.2。

blocks.en: Our image set for evaluation contains 105 105 generated images: 21 21 shared prompts submitted to Stable Diffusion 2.1 [ 1 ] , Qwen-Image-2.0 [ 29 ] , Midjourney [ 14 ] , GPT Image 2 [ 19 ] , and Nano Banana 2 [ 8 ] . Following prior work [ 32 ] , prompts span animal, object, document, human, scene, satellite, and face-portrait categories, with three prompts per category. GPT-4o-mini proposes prompts, which are manually reviewed. For each prompt–generator pair, we generate three candidates and manually select the highest-quality output. This controlled, curated set supports paired processing comparisons but does not represent the full distribution of generated images.
blocks.zh: 我们的评价图像集包含105个105个生成的图像:21个21个共享提示,提交给了稳定传播2.1[1],Quen-Image-2.0 [29],Midjourney [14],GPT图像2 [19],和Nano Banana 2 [8]. 在前作[32]后,提示横跨动物,物体,文件,人类,场景,卫星,和面相图等类别,每个类别有三个提示. GPT-4o-mini提出提示,经过人工审查. 每对即时生成者,我们产生三名候选人,并手动选择质量最高的产出。 此可控,可编程的集支持对等处理比较,但不代表生成的图像的完整分布.

blocks.en: Single-Tool Effectiveness
blocks.zh: 单一工具的效力

blocks.en: We apply the collected tools in our benchmark respectively on the evaluated 105 105 generated images on six state-of-the-art detectors. The summarized results are listed in Table 1 .
blocks.zh: 我们将收集的工具分别用于在六个最新探测器上评估的105-105出图像。 汇总结果见表1。

blocks.en:
The strongest single-tool ASRs in Table 1 range from 25.25 % 25.25\% against SIDA-13B to 100 % 100\% against AIDE .
The highest ASRs are 45.54 % 45.54\% for FakeVLM , 46.88 % 46.88\% for FakeShield , and 66.67 % 66.67\% for GPT-5.6-luna . These results demonstrate that in-the-wild malicious actors could find effective single tools through internet knowledge conversion.
blocks.zh:
表1中最强的单工具ASR从25.25%对SIDA-13B到100%对AIDE。
最高的ASR为:假VLM的45.54% 45.54%;假Shield的46.88% 46.88%;GPT-5.6-luna的66.67% 66.67%。 这些结果表明,在万能的恶意行为者可以通过互联网知识转换找到有效的单一工具。

blocks.en: Besides the best performed web-derived tools, there also exist a lot effective tools. Compared with the six selected academic baselines, each detectors are vulnerable to a set of web-derived tools whose ASR are higher. For example, over 10 10 tools achieves higher ASR than the best academic baselines for five evalauted detectors except FakeShield , but FakeShield also have 3 3 tools whose ASR is higher than 40 % 40\% . These results demonstrate that the effective tools are not rarely exist in the internet.
blocks.zh: 除了最佳的网络工具外,还有许多有效的工具。 与六个选定的学术基线相比,每个探测器都容易受到一套网络衍生工具的影响,这些工具的ASR较高。 例如,超过10个工具实现的ASR比5个被蒸发的探测器的最佳学术基线要高,但"假盾"(FakeShield)除外,而"假盾"(FakeShield)也有3个工具,其ASR高于40%的40\%. 这些结果表明,互联网上并非很少存在有效的工具。

blocks.en: Although our obtained tool bench contain serveral effective tools for detectors, not all of them are effective. Morevoer, tool performance are also different across different detectors. For example, print_rescan reaches 25.25 % 25.25\% against SIDA-13B and 3.96 % 3.96\% against FakeVLM .
blocks.zh: 尽管我们获得的工具长凳中包含了服务器有效的探测器工具,但并非所有工具都有效. Morevoer,工具性能在不同探测器之间也有所不同. 例如,print_rescan对SIDA-13B的评分达到25.25% 25.25%;对FakeVLM的评分为3.96% 3.96%。

blocks.en: Results on Combining Multiple Available Tools
blocks.zh: 关于合并多种可用工具的结果

blocks.en: Besides simply adopting single-tools, malicious attackers may collect several useful tools and combine them for effective attack. To explore such risks, we first select eight effective tools as the candidate pool, which are selected the top-2 effective tools based on its single performance on FakeVLM , SIDA-13B , FakeShield , CommForensics and AIDE . And then we select subsets of them, apply the tool set on the image and then evaluate on the detectors.
blocks.zh: 恶意攻击者除了简单地采用单工具外,还可能收集出几个有用的工具并结合起来进行有效攻击. 为了探索这些风险,我们首先选择8个有效的工具作为候选人才库,这些工具是根据其在FakeVLM,SIDA-13B,FakeShield,CompanyForensics和AIDE上的单一性能而选择的顶级-2有效工具. 然后我们选择它们的子集,在图像上应用工具集,然后对探测器进行评估.

blocks.en: Figure 3 shows that larger tool pools provide more opportunities to find combinations that change a detector’s decision. For FakeVLM , maximum coverage rises from 63.37 % 63.37\% with two available tools to 84.16 % 84.16\% with three and 92.08 % 92.08\% with four. Four-tool sets reach 68.69 % 68.69\% for SIDA-13B , 79.69 % 79.69\% for FakeShield , and 87.32 % 87.32\% for GPT-5.6-luna . CommForensics and AIDE both reach 100 % 100\% . With all eight tools available, coverage reaches 100 % 100\% for FakeVLM , exceeds 95 % 95\% for FakeShield and GPT-5.6-luna , and exceeds 80 % 80\% for SIDA-13B . These results show that tools derived from public knowledge can provide effective candidates for detector evasion.
blocks.zh: 图3显示,更大的工具库为寻找改变探测器决定的组合提供了更多机会。 对于假的VLM,最大覆盖率从63.37%的63.37%有两种可用的工具提高到84.16%的84.16%有3个工具,92.08%的92.08%有4个工具。 4个工具箱的SIDA-13B达到68.69% 68.69%,假盾达到79.69% 79.69%,GPT-5.6-luna达到87.32%。 共产主义和AIDE都达到了100%的100分. 有了所有8种工具,假VLM的覆盖率达到100%-100%;假Shield和GPT-5.6-luna的覆盖率超过95%-95%;SIDA-13B的覆盖率超过80%-80%。 这些结果显示,从公众知识中衍生出的工具可以为逃避探测器提供有效的候选者.

blocks.en: Table 3 also shows that effective combinations are common in this selected pool. More than half of the three-tool sets exceed 50 % 50\% ASR for FakeVLM , GPT-5.6-luna , CommForensics , and AIDE . For SIDA-13B , 12 of the 56 three-tool sets exceed that threshold. Among four-tool sets, at least 52 of 70 exceed 50 % 50\% ASR for every detector, and all 70 do so for FakeShield , GPT-5.6-luna , CommForensics , and AIDE . This suggests that attackers could combine publicly available techniques, translated into tools with an LLM, to find effective options against a range of detectors.
blocks.zh: 表3还显示,在这个选定的集合中,有效的组合是常见的。 超过半数的三工具组超过50%的ASR,用于假VLM、GPT-5.6-luna、Commerforensics和AIDE。 对于SIDA-13B,56个三工具组中有12个超过了这个阈值。 在四个工具箱中,每台探测器至少有52个超过50%的ASR,所有70个都用于假盾、GPT-5.6-luna、Commerforensics和AIDE。 这表明攻击者可以将可公开获得的技术与LLM结合,转化为工具,以针对一系列探测器找到有效的选择.

blocks.en: Observed Weaknesses of Current Detectors.
blocks.zh: 观测到当前探测器的弱点。

blocks.en: Our results also point to weaknesses that differ across detectors. Table 4 lists the categories of the strongest individual tools and highest-coverage sets.
blocks.zh: 我们的结果显示,各种探测器的弱点各不相同。 表4列出了最强的个人工具和最高覆盖的成套工具的类别。

blocks.en: The strongest single tools fall into different categories, suggesting that each detector responds differently to image processing. The strongest tools for FakeVLM and SIDA-13B use analog or capture effects, while those for FakeShield , GPT-5.6-luna , CommForensics , and AIDE use destylization, local-texture, color/white-balance, and resampling operations, respectively.
blocks.zh: 最强的单个工具属于不同的类别,说明每个探测器对图像处理的反应不同. FakeVLM和SIDA-13B的最强工具使用模拟或捕捉效果,而用于FakeShield,GPT-5.6-luna,Commerforensics,AIDE的则分别使用脱潮,局部纹理,颜色/白平衡和再生操作.

blocks.en: Figure 5 : Tool counts across ten assigned processing categories. Categories describe intended operations rather than verified perceptual improvements.
blocks.zh: 图5:工具计分10个指定处理类别。 类别描述的是预期行动,而不是经过核实的感知改进。

blocks.en:
Tool combinations also provide new perspectives on detector weaknesses because the strongest individual tool does not always be included in the best combination. For FakeVLM , the strongest three-tool set combines resampling, de-stylization, and detail recovery, reaching 84.16 % 84.16\% coverage. Adding composition raises coverage to 92.08 % 92.08\% in the strongest four-tool set. However, none of them include the original analog/capture technique.
Although the best combination attack in SIDA-13B includes its related strongest single-tool, results on tool combination more weaknesses of it, especially for the composition attack, which improves the ASR by 25 % 25\% when including it.
The strongest portfolios for FakeShield and GPT-5.6-luna also differ from their best individual tools. FakeShield ’s strongest single tool uses de-stylization, but its four-tool set spans composition, color/white balance, and analog/capture. For GPT-5.6-luna , local texture leads among single tools, while the strongest four-tool set includes composition, color/white balance, analog/capture, and detail recovery. These further reveals more weaknesses of current detectors. For CommForensics and AIDE , the strongest single tools point to color and resampling as useful stress tests, respectively, though other weaknesses may also exist.
blocks.zh:
工具组合还提供了探测器弱点的新视角,因为最强的单个工具并不总是包含在最佳组合中. 对于"假VLM",最强的"三工具"集结合了再生,去 Stylization,和细节恢复,覆盖率达到84.16% 84.16%. 在最强的4个工具组中,添加成分将覆盖率提高到92.08% 92.08%。 然而,它们中没有一个包括原始的模拟/抓取技术.
虽然SIDA-13B中最好的组合攻击包括了它相关的最强单工具,但工具组合上的结果更是其弱点,尤其是成分攻击,在将ASR包含在内时将ASR改进了25% 25.Q.
FakeShield和GPT-5.6-luna最强的组合也与其最好的个人工具不同. 假话 Shield最强的单一工具使用去斯泰尔化,但其四套工具跨越了组成、颜色/白色平衡和模拟/捕获。 对于GPT-5.6-luna,局部纹理在单个工具中领先,而最强的4个工具集包括组成,颜色/白色平衡,模拟/抓取,以及细节回收. 这些进一步揭示出目前探测器的更薄弱环节. 对于Commerforensics和AIDE,最强的单个工具分别指向色彩和再生作为有用的应力测试,尽管其他弱点也可能存在.

blocks.en: Together, these results point to detector-specific weaknesses and suggest directions for future improvements. They also show why web-sourced advice poses a broad risk: discussions span many aspects of image editing and photography, and can therefore yield tools that target different weaknesses across detectors.
blocks.zh: 这些结果共同表明检测器特有的弱点,并提出未来改进的方向。 它们也显示了网络来源的建议为何构成广泛的风险:讨论涉及图像编辑和摄影的许多方面,因此可以产生针对不同探测器弱点的工具。

blocks.en: Source-Level Effectiveness
blocks.zh: 源级有效性

blocks.en:
We summarize source membership among the strongest individual tools and highest-ASR tool sets in Table 5 .
AI image-tool sites contribute the strongest single tools for four detectors. Reddit provides the strongest single tool for SIDA-13B and appears in the highest-ASR sets for all six detectors.
Tech media provides the strongest single tool for GPT-5.6-luna .
These results show that these publicly accessible sources can also generate tools effective against different detectors, highlighting the potential reach of web-sourced risks.
In contrast, GitHub and diffusion-guidance sources have relatively high tool generation but do not appear in the reported highest-ASR sets. One possible explanation is that detector designers already consider techniques from these sources as they are more professional.
blocks.zh:
我们总结表5中最强的个人工具和最高ASR工具组的来源成员。
AI图像工具站点为四个探测器贡献了最强的单一工具. Reddit为SIDA-13B提供了最强的单一工具,并出现在所有6个探测器的最高ASR集中.

这些结果表明,这些可公开获取的来源也可以产生出对抗不同探测器的有效工具,凸显出网络来源风险的潜在范围.
相反地,GitHub和传播指导源具有较高的工具生成量,但没有出现在所报告的最高的ASR集中。 一种可能的解释是,探测器设计师已经考虑到这些来源的技术,因为这些技术更专业.

blocks.en: Engagement and Effectiveness.
blocks.zh: 参与和效力。

blocks.en:
Besides the analysis on attack effectiveness and sources, we also explores whether the relationship between the source engagement and the effectiveness of the extracted tools. Since not all sources have the engagement score, we only provide some case study in this section.
In the Reddit case study, natural_color_correction comes from a thread with 56 56 upvotes and reaches 75.00 % 75.00\% ASR against CommForensics .
A tool from a post with zero upvotes and 20 20 comments, upscale_grain_denoise , reaches 91.67 % 91.67\% . These examples show that more engagement may be related to the effectiveness of the extracted tools which should pay more attention as a defender.
blocks.zh:
除了对攻击有效性和来源的分析外,我们还探讨了来源接触与被取出的工具的有效性之间的关系。 由于并非所有来源都有参与得分,我们只在本节提供一些案例研究。
在Reddit案例研究中,自然_color_recorization来自一条线,有56个56个高票,对准Comforensics达到75.00% 75.00% ASR.
来自一个零升票和 20 个评论的工具, 这些例子表明,更多的参与可能与所取出的工具的有效性有关,这些工具应当作为维护者给予更多的关注。

blocks.en: Conclusion
blocks.zh: 结论

blocks.en: We present WildFakeToolBench , a collection of 156 156 executable image-processing tools derived from 220 220 public sources across 142 142 domains. The tools run on CPUs, retain their source evidence, and are synthesized and validated without detector feedback.
blocks.zh: 由来自142个领域的220个公共来源的156个可执行图像处理工具。 这些工具运行在CPU上,保留出自其出处的证据,并在没有探测器反馈的情况下被合成和验证.

blocks.en: We evaluate the tools on 105 105 images from five generators against six detectors. Every detector is vulnerable to at least one tool. The strongest individual tools achieve ASRs from 25.25 % 25.25\% to 100 % 100\% and exceed the strongest of six selected baselines for each detector. An eight-tool pool achieves candidate coverage above 80 % 80\% for all six detectors. Effectiveness varies by detector, and high coverage does not ensure one-shot evasion. These findings show that web-sourced knowledge can complement researcher-selected robustness evaluations.
blocks.zh: 我们用五台发电机的105到105个图像 对六台探测器进行评估 每个探测器都至少容易受到一个工具的伤害. 最强的单个工具实现ASR从25.25% 25.25%-100% 100-%,并超过每个探测器六个选定基准中最强. 8个工具池实现所有6个探测器候选人覆盖率超过80% 80%。 有效性因探测器而异,高覆盖率并不能保证一发而逃. 这些调查结果表明,网络来源的知识可以补充研究人员选定的强性评价。

blocks.en: Ethics Considerations
blocks.zh: 道德考虑

blocks.en:
This work has clear dual-use implications. The transformations collected and
synthesized by WildFake can help researchers identify weaknesses in
AI-image detectors, but they can also be used to make generated images harder
to detect. We therefore present these tools as a robustness-evaluation resource
intended for authorized defensive research and detector development.

这项工作具有明显的双重用途影响。 收集的转化和
由"野生假冒"合成,可以帮助研究人员发现其中的弱点.
AI-图像探测器,但也可以用来使生成的图像更难
用来侦测 因此,我们将这些工具作为强有力的评价资源

and we evaluate the resulting tools in a controlled setting on an AI-generated

reduce, but do not eliminate, the potential risks associated with releasing a
dual-use evaluation resource.

blocks.en: Appendix A Construction Details
blocks.zh: 附录A 建筑细节

blocks.en: WildFake constructs the tool benchmark through retrieval, method extraction and deduplication, code synthesis, and validation. Figure 1 presents the benchmark overview; the detailed construction procedure is documented below.
blocks.zh: WildFake通过检索,方法提取和分解,代码合成和验证来构建工具基准. 图1列出基准概况;详细施工程序如下:

blocks.en: Retrieval and Corpus Processing
blocks.zh: 检索和公司处理

blocks.en: GPT-4o-mini assists with queries covering explicit detector-evasion advice and indirect photography knowledge. Tavily retrieves up to five results per query, including URLs and page text. Platform-specific searches supplement general search for Reddit and X. Collection is limited to public web content; this restriction does not itself determine the licensing of retrieved material. Query strings appear in Appendix E.1 .
blocks.zh: GPT-4o-mini协助查询,包括明确的探测器避去建议和间接摄影知识. Tavily每次查询获取最多5个结果,包括URL和页面文本. 平台专用搜索是对Reddit和X的一般搜索的补充. Collection仅限于公共网络内容;这一限制本身并不决定对被检索出的材料的许可. 查询字符串见附录E.1。

blocks.en: We discard pages with fewer than 300 300 extracted characters, remove exact-URL duplicates, and suppress domains primarily returning videos, marketplace listings, or other non-text content. Each normalized Post record stores a stable identifier, page text, URL, domain, matched discourse category, originating query, and available retrieval metadata. Source records support provenance and the source-level analysis.
blocks.zh: 我们丢弃不到300300个取出字符的网页,删除精确的URL重复,并压制主要返回视频、市场列表或其他非文本内容的域。 每个正常 后作记录存储一个稳定的标识符,页面文本,URL,域名,匹配的会话类别,发端查询,以及可用的检索元数据. 来源记录支持出处和来源级分析.

blocks.en: Method Extraction and Deduplication
blocks.zh: 采掘和复制方法

blocks.en: GPT-4o-mini examines sources for actionable processing ideas and their stated mechanisms, retaining quoted evidence. The extraction prompt is reproduced in Appendix E.2 . Methods need not specify exact numeric parameters, since synthesis subsequently supplies concrete implementations.
blocks.zh: GPT-4o-mini审查可采取行动的处理想法的来源及其申明的机制,保留所引用的证据。 提取提示见附录E.2。 方法不需要具体指明确切的数字参数,因为合成随后提供了具体的执行。

blocks.en: Deduplication distinguishes repeated concrete techniques from related operations. For example, film-grain overlays and sensor-noise injection need not be merged merely because both add noise. Our deduplication procedure first groups duplicates within batches, then uses compact method summaries for a global pass. Candidate duplicate groups are checked for functional similarity, including comparison of generated implementations. Overlapping verified groups are merged by transitive closure, retaining one representative and source provenance. The duplicate-detection and mechanism-grouping prompts are distinguished in Appendix E.3 .
blocks.zh: 重复法将重复的混凝土技术与相关的操作区分开来. 例如,胶片-胶片上盖和传感器-噪声注射不一定仅仅因为两者都增加了噪音而合并. 我们的分解程序首先分批重复,然后使用紧凑的方法摘要进行全局通行。 对候选的重复组进行功能相似性检查,包括比较产生的执行。 通过暂时关闭、保留一名代表和来源地,将经过核实的重叠组合并。 附录E.3对重复探测和机制分组提示作了区分。

blocks.en: Tool Interface and Admission Checks
blocks.zh: 工具接口和录入检查

blocks.en: GPT-4o-mini converts each retained idea into a Python class with an image-processing method, a parameter schema, and usage guidance. Implementations use common numeric image-processing libraries and do not load a neural image-editing model. The supplied synthesis prompt prohibits importing PyTorch. Parameters control properties such as noise strength, rotation, and blur; image-specific settings are proposed later during evaluation.
blocks.zh: GPT-4o-mini将每个保留的想法转换为Python类,具有图像处理方法,参数schema,以及用法指导. 执行使用常见的数字图像处理库,不装入神经图像编辑模型. 所提供合成快取禁止导入PyTorch. 参数控制噪音强度,旋转等属性,并模糊;稍后在评价期间提出图像特定设置.

blocks.en: Checks test syntax, the class/interface and parameter dictionary, execution on a fixed validation image, non-identity output, and SSIM-based output distortion. When validation fails, the code and diagnostic are returned to the LLM, with at most three generation attempts per method. The validation image and synthesis prompt are documented in Appendix E.4 . Validation errors provide software feedback; no detector score or decision is used to repair or admit tools.
blocks.zh: 检查测试语法,类/界面和参数词典,在固定的验证图像上执行,非身份输出,以及基于SSIM的输出扭曲. 当验证失败时,代码和诊断返回LLM,每个方法最多有三代尝试. 验证图像和合成快报载于附录E.4。 验证错误提供软件反馈;没有检测器分数或决定用于修复或接纳工具.

blocks.en: From Public Sources to Executable Tools
blocks.zh: 从公共来源到可执行工具

blocks.en: The collection contains 220 220 sources across 142 142 domains. Method mining labels 77 77 sources valuable and 143 143 discard, with no borderline assignments, and extracts 204 204 method records. Deduplication removes 35 35 redundant records and leaves 169 169 records; code synthesis and validation admit 156 156 tools, approximately 92 % 92\% of the deduplicated methods. Of the 13 13 failures, five produce identity outputs and eight fail to yield runnable implementations within three attempts. This shows that informal advice can often be converted into executable processing, while also revealing limitations of method extraction and code translation. Conversion success does not imply detector evasion.
blocks.zh: 该汇编包含142 142个领域的220个来源。 方法开采标签为77个有价值来源和143个丢弃物,无分界线任务,并提取出204 204方法记录。 复制删除了35个35个冗余记录,留下了169个169个记录;代码合成和验证接纳了156个工具,大约92%的92\%被复制的方法. 在这13起失败中,有5起是身份鉴定产出,有8起是三次尝试中无法完成的。 这表明非正式的建议往往可以被转化为可执行的处理,同时也揭示出方法提取和代码翻译的局限性. 转换成功并不意味着探测器逃避。

blocks.en: Appendix B Tool Category Definitions
blocks.zh: 附录B 工具类别

blocks.en:
• Detail Recovery & Artifact Repair These tools restore local details that image generators often smooth out.
Typical operations add edge variation, repair blurred regions, and reduce

blocks.en: FakeVLM [ 32 ] It fine-tunes a LLaVA-1.5-7B on their collected 100 100 k-image dataset annotated with natural-language artifact clues. Thereby, it can enable the VLM’s ability of reasoning to spot the fake features and then recognize the fake images with explanations. SIDA-13B [ 13 ] It fine-tunes LISA to emit a classification token and a segmentation token from one forward pass. Then the model can not only classify the fake images, but also localize the patterns of the fake images. Such segmentation ability also helps its classification. FakeShield [ 34 ] It contains two separately-trained modules: DTE-FDM concatenates a domain-tag classifier’s output with image tokens and feeds an LLM for real/fake judgment and explanation; MFLM then takes that explanation plus image tokens to produce a SAM-aligned tamper mask. We only use DTE-FDM for verdict. CommForensics [ 21 ] It fine-tunes a CLIP-ViT-S backbone to build a binary classifier with 2.7 2.7 M images sampled from 4803 4803 generators. AIDE [ 35 ] It is a mixture-of-experts detector: DCT-based patch scoring selects the highest- and lowest-frequency patches, whose SRM noise residual is each fed to a dedicated fine-tuned ResNet-50. Moreover, it also combines a separately fine-tuned ConvNeXt-based OpenCLIP branch encodes the whole image or global semantics. Finally, all three pooled features are concatenated into an MLP for the final score. GPT-5.6-luna [ 20 ] A hosted vision-language model evaluated by direct prompting. We directly prompt the image and prompt them to classify the image, the prompt is listed in Appendix E.6 .

blocks.en:
The analyzer uses the following prompt to identify actionable methods and retain
their supporting evidence from each retrieved source. \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨You are mining a community post (Reddit thread or blog/forum article) for IDEAS \iow_now:Ne ¨that could make AI-generated images pass as real photographs and thereby evade \iow_now:Ne ¨VLM-based fake-image detectors (FakeVLM, FakeShield, SIDA). \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨WHAT WE WANT – the IDEA, not a finished recipe. \iow_now:Ne ¨We are NOT asking for exact PIL/OpenCV parameters. We want the *concept* and the \iow_now:Ne ¨*mechanism*: the intuition a practitioner described for why an AI image looks fake \iow_now:Ne ¨and what they do about it. A downstream coding agent will turn each idea into a \iow_now:Ne ¨concrete tool later. Example of a good extraction: \iow_now:Ne ¨  idea: "photograph or re-scan the AI image at a slight tilt, like a phone snapshot \iow_now:Ne ¨         of a printout" \iow_now:Ne ¨  mechanism: "introduces perspective skew, re-photography sensor noise and JPEG \iow_now:Ne ¨              history that real shared photos have but clean AI renders lack" \iow_now:Ne ¨That is fully acceptable EVEN THOUGH no exact rotation angle is given. \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨A method may be a single step or many steps – STEP COUNT DOES NOT MATTER. \iow_now:Ne ¨Do NOT discard an idea just because it is "only one operation". Judge ideas by \iow_now:Ne ¨NOVELTY and FEASIBILITY (defined below), not by complexity. \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨CLASSIFY each extracted idea into one method_type: \iow_now:Ne ¨  - "generative" : uses a generative model to do the work – T2I/img2img prompt \iow_now:Ne ¨                   tricks, negative prompts, low-denoise regeneration, LoRA/ \iow_now:Ne ¨                   checkpoint swaps, diffusion inpainting of artifacts. \iow_now:Ne ¨  - "numeric"    : a deterministic signal/pixel operation or pipeline – grain, \iow_now:Ne ¨                   compression, sensor-noise, color/tone, geometric, capture-pipeline \iow_now:Ne ¨                   mimicry. No neural model needed at apply time. \iow_now:Ne ¨  - "hybrid"     : explicitly combines the two (e.g. numeric pipeline THEN a \iow_now:Ne ¨                   generative regeneration pass, or generate-then-launder). \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨SKIP only genuinely empty content: venting, news/ethics commentary, pure \iow_now:Ne ¨"is this fake?" guessing with no technique, or vague aesthetic praise with no \iow_now:Ne ¨actionable mechanism. Set verdict="discard" and candidate_methods=[] for those. \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨Score the POST on three axes (1=worst, 10=best): \iow_now:Ne ¨  - novelty     : how unusual / under-the-radar are these ideas? Favor techniques a \iow_now:Ne ¨                  detector is UNLIKELY to have been trained against (recent tricks, \iow_now:Ne ¨                  niche capture pipelines, creative model-side moves). Common, \iow_now:Ne ¨                  obvious moves score low; clever or fresh ideas score high. \iow_now:Ne ¨  - feasibility : could an LLM coding agent realistically implement these as an \iow_now:Ne ¨                  image tool? (a PIL/OpenCV op, or a call to a local generative \iow_now:Ne ¨                  model). Concrete, mechanism-clear ideas score high; hand-wavy or \iow_now:Ne ¨                  research-grade ("train a new GAN") ideas score low. \iow_now:Ne ¨  - relevance   : does the content actually concern making AI images look real / \iow_now:Ne ¨                  evading detection (vs. unrelated photo editing)? \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨For each candidate idea capture: \iow_now:Ne ¨  - name (snake_case, ˜2-4 words) \iow_now:Ne ¨  - idea (one sentence: the concept) \iow_now:Ne ¨  - mechanism (one sentence: WHY it makes the image look real / why a detector \iow_now:Ne ¨    might miss it) \iow_now:Ne ¨  - method_type ("generative" | "numeric" | "hybrid") \iow_now:Ne ¨  - quoted_evidence (exact phrase you took it from, <= 200 chars) \iow_now:Ne ¨  - source ("post" | "comment_<author>") \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨Output ONLY valid JSON, schema: \iow_now:Ne ¨{ \iow_now:Ne ¨  "post_id": "<echo>", \iow_now:Ne ¨  "verdict": "valuable" | "borderline" | "discard", \iow_now:Ne ¨  "scores": { \iow_now:Ne ¨    "novelty": <int 1-10>, \iow_now:Ne ¨    "feasibility": <int 1-10>, \iow_now:Ne ¨    "relevance": <int 1-10> \iow_now:Ne ¨  }, \iow_now:Ne ¨  "overall_value": <int 1-10>, \iow_now:Ne ¨  "rationale": "<2-3 sentences>", \iow_now:Ne ¨  "candidate_methods": [ \iow_now:Ne ¨    { \iow_now:Ne ¨      "name": "…", \iow_now:Ne ¨      "idea": "…", \iow_now:Ne ¨      "mechanism": "…", \iow_now:Ne ¨      "method_type": "generative" | "numeric" | "hybrid", \iow_now:Ne ¨      "quoted_evidence": "…", \iow_now:Ne ¨      "source": "…" \iow_now:Ne ¨    } \iow_now:Ne ¨  ] \iow_now:Ne ¨} \iow_now:Ne ¨ Method-Mining Prompt Deduplication Prompts Batch Deduplication Prompt. The following prompt identifies duplicate methods within each processing batch. \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨You are given a flat list of specific attack-method ideas (each already \iow_now:Ne ¨individually catalogued), pooled from several independent batches. Because \iow_now:Ne ¨each batch was processed separately, the SAME concrete technique may appear \iow_now:Ne ¨more than once under slightly different names/wordings. \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨Your ONLY job: find groups of ids that describe the SAME concrete technique \iow_now:Ne ¨(near-identical concept and mechanism – not just the same broad theme). \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨BE CONSERVATIVE. Two methods are duplicates only if a downstream coding agent \iow_now:Ne ¨would end up writing essentially the same tool for both of them. Methods that \iow_now:Ne ¨are merely related or thematically similar (e.g. "film grain overlay" vs. \iow_now:Ne ¨"sensor noise injection" vs. "print re-scan blur") are NOT duplicates – leave \iow_now:Ne ¨them ungrouped. If you are not confident two ids are the same technique, do \iow_now:Ne ¨not group them. \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨Do not invent new ids. Do not include singleton groups (a group only makes \iow_now:Ne ¨sense with >= 2 members). Most ids will not appear in any group – that is \iow_now:Ne ¨expected and correct. \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨Output ONLY valid JSON, schema: \iow_now:Ne ¨{ \iow_now:Ne ¨  "duplicate_groups": [ \iow_now:Ne ¨    ["m3", "m17", "m42"], \iow_now:Ne ¨    ["m8", "m55"] \iow_now:Ne ¨  ] \iow_now:Ne ¨} \iow_now:Ne ¨ Batch Deduplication Prompt Mechanism-Grouping Prompt. The following archived prompt groups deduplicated methods into higher-level mechanism categories. \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨You are given the FINAL deduplicated list of specific attack-method ideas \iow_now:Ne ¨(for making AI-generated images pass as real / evade VLM fake-image \iow_now:Ne ¨detectors). Each has already been individually catalogued and scored \iow_now:Ne ¨elsewhere – you are not re-scoring or dropping any of them here. \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨Your job: group these specific methods into a smaller set of GENERALIZED / \iow_now:Ne ¨ARCHETYPE methods – higher-level strategies that explain WHY a cluster of \iow_now:Ne ¨specific methods works (the shared mechanism), for use in reporting and \iow_now:Ne ¨strategy selection. This is an ADDITIONAL summary layer on top of the \iow_now:Ne ¨specific list, not a replacement for it – every specific method stays in the \iow_now:Ne ¨specific list regardless of which cluster it lands in here. \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨Guidelines: \iow_now:Ne ¨  - Produce however many clusters naturally fit the data – typically \iow_now:Ne ¨    somewhere in the 6-15 range for ˜100-150 specific methods, fewer if the \iow_now:Ne ¨    pool is smaller. Do not force a fixed count. \iow_now:Ne ¨  - Every specific method should belong to exactly one cluster. A method that \iow_now:Ne ¨    is genuinely singular (no others share its mechanism) may form a \iow_now:Ne ¨    cluster of one – that’s fine, don’t force it into a bad fit. \iow_now:Ne ¨  - Name each cluster for the shared MECHANISM (e.g. "capture_pipeline_mimicry", \iow_now:Ne ¨    "signal_domain_texture_injection", "semantic_prompt_evasion"), not for a \iow_now:Ne ¨    single member’s name. \iow_now:Ne ¨  - ‘member_names‘ must reference the exact ‘name‘ field of specific methods \iow_now:Ne ¨    from the input list. \iow_now:Ne ¨  - ‘priority‘ for a cluster = the max priority among its members (rounded to \iow_now:Ne ¨    1 decimal). \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨Output ONLY valid JSON, schema: \iow_now:Ne ¨{ \iow_now:Ne ¨  "generalized_methods": [ \iow_now:Ne ¨    { \iow_now:Ne ¨      "name": "snake_case_cluster_name", \iow_now:Ne ¨      "description": "<1-2 sentences: the shared mechanism/strategy>", \iow_now:Ne ¨      "member_names": ["specific_method_a", "specific_method_b"], \iow_now:Ne ¨      "priority": <float, 1 decimal> \iow_now:Ne ¨    } \iow_now:Ne ¨  ] \iow_now:Ne ¨} \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨ Mechanism-Grouping Prompt Tool Synthesis and Validation Tool-Synthesis Prompt. The following prompt converts each retained method into a runnable
image-processing tool that follows the framework’s common interface. \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨You are a Python engineer implementing an image-manipulation tool for an \iow_now:Ne ¨adversarial-attack research framework. You are given a single ADVERSARIAL IDEA \iow_now:Ne ¨mined from a community blog/forum (concept + mechanism), and you must turn it \iow_now:Ne ¨into a concrete, runnable tool. \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨The tool defeats a fake-image detector by post-processing an AI-generated image \iow_now:Ne ¨so it reads as a real photograph. Implement the IDEA faithfully – choose sensible \iow_now:Ne ¨concrete operations and parameter ranges yourself; the idea gives you the concept, \iow_now:Ne ¨you supply the realization. \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨You MUST output a single, self-contained Python module that defines ONE class \iow_now:Ne ¨subclassing ‘BaseTool‘. Follow this exact contract: \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨“‘python \iow_now:Ne ¨from typing import Dict, Any \iow_now:Ne ¨from PIL import Image \iow_now:Ne ¨import numpy as np \iow_now:Ne ¨# you may also import: scipy.ndimage, scipy.signal, math, random  (all available) \iow_now:Ne ¨# DO NOT import torch – numpy + PIL + scipy . \iow_now:Ne ¨from .base_tool import BaseTool \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨class <CamelCaseName>Tool(BaseTool): \iow_now:Ne ¨    def __init__(self): \iow_now:Ne ¨        super().__init__( \iow_now:Ne ¨            name="<snake_case_name>",                 # MUST match the given name \iow_now:Ne ¨            description="<what the transform does, effect-only, 1-3 sentences>", \iow_now:Ne ¨        ) \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨    def apply(self, image: Image.Image, params: Dict[str, Any]) -> Image.Image: \iow_now:Ne ¨        self.validate_params(params) \iow_now:Ne ¨        # read params with .get(name, default); convert image to RGB if needed; \iow_now:Ne ¨        # operate via numpy/PIL/scipy/cv2; return a NEW PIL.Image (mode "RGB"). \iow_now:Ne ¨        … \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨    def get_param_schema(self) -> Dict[str, Any]: \iow_now:Ne ¨        # 1-4 params, each: {"type": "int|float|str", "min":.., "max":.., \iow_now:Ne ¨        #                    "description":.., "default":.., "required": False} \iow_now:Ne ¨        … \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨    def get_guidance(self) -> str: \iow_now:Ne ¨        return "<one line: parameter ranges + when this tool is most useful>" \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨“‘ \iow_now:Ne ¨ Prompt for Tool Synthesis Validation Image and Retry Procedure. The test image is not iid noise. A 24 × 24 24\times 24 uniform random field is
bicubically upsampled to 512 × 512 512\times 512 and a σ = 8 \sigma=8 Gaussian grain is added
on top, under a fixed RandomState(42) . The reason is on pure iid noise there is no spatial correlation for a blur,
geometric or texture-matching operation to preserve, so SSIM measurement cannot be done. If validation
fails, the generated tool and the failure reason are returned to the LLM for
revision. We allow at most 3 3 generation attempts per method. Tool-Parameter Selection Prompt The following prompt asks GPT-4o-mini to select five image-specific parameter
settings that span the applicable strength range of a tool. \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨You are proposing parameter settings for an image-editing tool, to test how a fake-image detector responds to different intensities of the SAME tool applied to the SAME image. \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨Tool: {tool.name} \iow_now:Ne ¨Description: {tool.description} \iow_now:Ne ¨Parameters: {_param_desc(tool)} \iow_now:Ne ¨Usage guidance: {guidance} \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨You will be shown ONE image. Look at it and propose exactly {N_CANDIDATES} DIVERGING candidate parameter settings for this tool, spanning a clear intensity range from very light to very strong. Each candidate must be genuinely different (not near-duplicate values) so together they explore the tool’s effective range on this specific image. The test image is not iid noise. A 24 × 24 24\times 24 uniform random field is
bicubically upsampled to 512 × 512 512\times 512 and a σ = 8 \sigma=8 Gaussian grain is added
on top, under a fixed RandomState(42) . The reason is on pure iid noise there is no spatial correlation for a blur,
geometric or texture-matching operation to preserve, so SSIM measurement cannot be done. If validation
fails, the generated tool and the failure reason are returned to the LLM for
revision. We allow at most 3 3 generation attempts per method.

settings that span the applicable strength range of a tool. \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨You are proposing parameter settings for an image-editing tool, to test how a fake-image detector responds to different intensities of the SAME tool applied to the SAME image. \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨Tool: {tool.name} \iow_now:Ne ¨Description: {tool.description} \iow_now:Ne ¨Parameters: {_param_desc(tool)} \iow_now:Ne ¨Usage guidance: {guidance} \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨You will be shown ONE image. Look at it and propose exactly {N_CANDIDATES} DIVERGING candidate parameter settings for this tool, spanning a clear intensity range from very light to very strong. Each candidate must be genuinely different (not near-duplicate values) so together they explore the tool’s effective range on this specific image. Base your choices on what you can see in the image (e.g. its existing quality, texture, lighting) as well as the tool’s guidance above. \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨IMPORTANT: even "very_strong" must stay a PLAUSIBLE edit – the image must still look like a real, undamaged photo afterward. Do not propose settings so extreme that they visibly destroy the image (heavy artifacting, unrecognizable content, obvious tampering). A candidate that wrecks image quality will be discarded during evaluation regardless of whether it fools the detector, so there is no benefit to being overly aggressive – stay within the range where the edit could plausibly pass as an unedited photo to a human viewer. \iow_now:Ne ¨ \iow_now:Ne ¨Respond with ONLY valid JSON, no other text: \iow_now:Ne ¨{"candidates": [ \iow_now:Ne ¨  {"tier": "very_light", "params": {…}, "reasoning": "…"}, \iow_now:Ne ¨  {"tier": "light", "params": {…}, "reasoning": "…"}, \iow_now:Ne ¨  {"tier": "moderate", "params": {…}, "reasoning": "…"}, \iow_now:Ne ¨  {"tier": "strong", "params": {…}, "reasoning": "…"}, \iow_now:Ne ¨  {"tier": "very_strong", "params": {…}, "reasoning": "…"} \iow_now:Ne ¨]} Tool-Parameter Selection Prompt GPT-Based Detector Prompt The following prompt is used to obtain a binary real/fake judgment and a

Use the full 0-100 range and mean it: 90+ only with a clear artifact you can name, 50 for genuinely ambiguous, 10 or below when the image carries positive signs of real capture.
